title: Counting by status with COUNTIF
summary: Count how many stores are open, closed or being renovated with COUNTIF, using text and cell-reference criteria.

blocks.text: Head office wants a quick status check: how many stores are trading, how many are closed and how many are being renovated? The store list has a Status column, but counting by eye invites mistakes.
COUNTIF counts the cells in a range that meet a condition. It answers "how many?", while SUMIF answers "how much?".

items: Objective: count rows that match a condition with COUNTIF.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: Count the cells in range that meet criteria. There is no third argument: COUNTIF counts the rows, it does not add numbers.
Count the cells in B2:B8 that say Closed. Nyali and Likoni match, so the answer is 2.

items: Upper and lower case do not matter: "closed" counts Closed.
Point at a cell to avoid retyping, for example =COUNTIF($B$2:$B$8,E2) when E2 holds the word Renovation.
"<>Open" means not equal to Open. It counts every cell that is anything other than Open.
When nothing matches, COUNTIF returns 0, not an error.
Use $ signs on the range when you copy the formula down.

blocks.text: Use the store list from Training (A1:B8). Type whole numbers, for example 3.

items: COUNTIF(range, criteria) counts the cells that meet the criteria.
"<>Open" counts everything that is not Open.
A cell reference as criteria lets one formula be copied down a list of statuses.
No match returns 0, never an error.

blocks.text: A status summary that took ten minutes of counting now updates by itself when the store list changes.

items.prompt: No store in the list has the status "Relocated". What does =COUNTIF(B2:B8,"Relocated") show?
You want the number of order lines for Nairobi, not their value in KES. Which function fits?

options.label: COUNTIF, because you want how many lines
SUMIF, because it also looks at one column
AVERAGE, because it summarises a list
IF, because it tests one cell
